title: Permission
description:
A Permission is a reified authorization — the product-layer parallel to operational Membership. Following the Actor › Action › Resource model (as in AWS Cedar), it binds a `principal` (a User), a `role` (the capacity / action-set), and a `scope` (the Resource slot — a namespaced entity reference). Permission is a resource type (a node), not a bare edge, so the `grants` relationship has a node to point at.

Derive-first / author-fallback: the business→product projection materializes a Permission (and its `grants` edge back to the backing Membership) from operational Membership + access Rules. A Permission MAY also be hand-authored when no backing Membership exists (e.g. a service account), in which case it carries no `grants` edge. Identity is the tuple {principal, role, scope}, so a derived Permission reconciles onto a matching authored one rather than duplicating it.

name.description: Optional human-readable name for this Permission.

principal.description: The User this Permission is granted to — the Cedar principal. References a product User by name.

role.description: The Role (capacity / action-set) the principal exercises. References a product Role by name.

scope.description: The Resource slot — a single Cedar-style `::`-delimited qualified entity reference of arbitrary nesting depth, pointing at an entity that already exists (the product projection of an operational Group, or any Resource). NOT a separate Scope type; a reference. Examples: 'Alloc8::Groups::P&T', 'Alloc8::Groups::P&T::Subteam::Platform'.

grant_reason.description: Optional provenance: why this Permission exists. For a derived Permission this echoes the backing Membership; for an authored Permission it documents the out-of-band justification.
examples: Holds the Head position in the P&T group

examples.name: KyleApproverPandT
examples.grant_reason: Holds the Head position in the P&T group
